symbols.name: first integer
symbols.meaning: An integer, not both zero, that is the first argument of the gcd.
symbols.quote: Here $\gamma$ and $\rho$ are integers; the letters change meaning from their scalar and exponent uses on other pages.

symbols.name: second integer
symbols.meaning: An integer, not both zero, that is the second argument of the gcd.
symbols.quote: Here $\gamma$ and $\rho$ are integers; the letters change meaning from their scalar and exponent uses on other pages.

symbols.name: family member
symbols.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

symbols.name: family size
symbols.meaning: The number of members of the family, the count of integers in it.
symbols.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

symbols.name: member index
symbols.meaning: An index running over $1,\dots,J$ that numbers the members of the family.
symbols.quote: For a family $f_1,\dots,f_J$ of integers, $J$ is the number of members and $f_\sigma$ is the $\sigma$-th member, with $\sigma$ running over $1,\dots,J$ (the letters $f$ and $\sigma$ change meaning here).

symbols.name: second member index
symbols.meaning: A second index of a family member, distinct from $\sigma$ in the pairwise condition.
symbols.quote: The family is pairwise coprime when $\gcd(f_\sigma,f_{\sigma'})=1$ for all distinct indices $\sigma,\sigma'$.

symbols.name: common multiple candidate
symbols.meaning: An integer that is tested for divisibility by the product of the integers it is divided by.
symbols.quote: Two facts follow. First, if $\gamma$ and $\rho$ both divide an integer $Y$ and $\gcd(\gamma,\rho)=1$, then $\gamma\rho$ divides $Y$.

symbols.name: further integer
symbols.meaning: A further integer, coprime to $\rho$ in the same way that $\gamma$ is.
symbols.quote: Second, if $\gcd(\gamma,\rho)=\gcd(\gamma',\rho)=1$ for a further integer $\gamma'$, then $\gcd(\gamma\gamma',\rho)=1$.

symbols.name: Bézout coefficient
symbols.meaning: An integer with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, one of the Bézout coefficients of $\gamma$ and $\rho$.
symbols.quote: [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\Xi,\Psi$ (Bézout coefficients) with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, so $Y=\gamma(Y\Xi)+\rho(Y\Psi)$.

symbols.name: second Bézout coefficient
symbols.meaning: An integer with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, the coefficient of $\rho$ in that identity.
symbols.quote: [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) gives integers $\Xi,\Psi$ (Bézout coefficients) with $\gamma\Xi+\rho\Psi=1$, so $Y=\gamma(Y\Xi)+\rho(Y\Psi)$.

symbols.name: coefficient for further integer
symbols.meaning: An integer with $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$, the coefficient of $\gamma'$ in that identity.
symbols.quote: With $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$ for integers $\Xi',\Psi'$, multiplying the two identities gives $\gamma\gamma'(\Xi\Xi')+\rho(\cdots)=1$.

symbols.name: coefficient of rho
symbols.meaning: An integer with $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$, the coefficient of $\rho$ in that identity.
symbols.quote: With $\gamma'\Xi'+\rho\Psi'=1$ for integers $\Xi',\Psi'$, multiplying the two identities gives $\gamma\gamma'(\Xi\Xi')+\rho(\cdots)=1$.

symbols.name: family product
symbols.meaning: The product $f_1\cdots f_J$ of all members of the family.
symbols.quote: Let $\Pi=f_1\cdots f_J$ be the product of the family.

symbols.name: integers modulo f
symbols.meaning: The integers modulo $f$, whose elements are classes of integers that differ by multiples of $f$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathbb{Z}/f$ be the integers modulo $f$, whose classes hold integers differing by multiples of $f$.

symbols.name: tuple group
symbols.meaning: The group of tuples $(x_1,\dots,x_J)$ with $x_\sigma$ in $\mathbb{Z}/f_\sigma$, under entrywise addition.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}/f_1\times\cdots\times\mathbb{Z}/f_J$ be the group of tuples under entrywise addition; it has $\Pi$ elements.

symbols.name: all-ones tuple
symbols.meaning: The tuple $(1,\dots,1)$, with entry 1 in every place.

symbols.name: prefix product
symbols.meaning: The product of the first $\sigma-1$ members of the family, with $\Pi_1=1$.
symbols.quote: The split uses the prefix products $\Pi_\sigma=f_1\cdots f_{\sigma-1}$, with $\Pi_1=1$.

symbols.name: inverse multiplier
symbols.meaning: An integer that is an inverse of $\Pi_\sigma$ modulo $f_\sigma$, equal to the coefficient $\Xi$ of $\Pi_\sigma$.
symbols.quote: Each $\Pi_\sigma$ is coprime to $f_\sigma$, so $\Pi_\sigma\Xi+f_\sigma\Psi=1$ for some integers, and $\Upsilon_\sigma=\Xi$ satisfies $\Pi_\sigma\Upsilon_\sigma\equiv1\pmod{f_\sigma}$.

relations.predicate: lets cyclic axes combine into one
relations.quote: Coprimality of the lengths lets several cyclic axes combine into one [transform axis](transform-axis.md) of their product length.
